import cv2,numpy as np
im=cv2.imread('first_frame.png').astype(np.float32)
out=im.copy()
def fill(center, src_shift, axes, angle, blur=21):
 global out
 H,W=out.shape[:2]
 m=np.zeros((H,W),np.float32)
 cv2.ellipse(m,center,axes,angle,0,360,1,-1)
 m=cv2.GaussianBlur(m,(0,0),blur)
 # translate image source: dst(x,y)=im(x+dx,y+dy)
 dx,dy=src_shift
 M=np.float32([[1,0,dx],[0,1,dy]])
 src=cv2.warpAffine(im,M,(W,H),flags=cv2.INTER_LINEAR,borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REFLECT)
 # local color match in region surrounding, compare blurred source to blurred original near boundary/region
 # simply per-channel mean match under mask
 ring=(m>.05)&(m<.25)
 if ring.sum():
  delta=np.median(out[ring]-src[ring],axis=0)
  src+=delta
 out=out*(1-m[...,None])+src*m[...,None]
fill((555,365),(0,150),(145,72),-8,13)
fill((880,211),(0,150),(135,65),-9,13)
cv2.imwrite('.tmp/alpha_bg.png',np.clip(out,0,255).astype(np.uint8))
